name: sumly
description: Revenue, costs and visitors of your own projects, from your payment providers and your sites, with the changes Sumly's pages offer.

interface.longDescription: Sumly is revenue and visitor analytics for people who sell software, apps and online products: it shows MRR, revenue, costs and where paying customers come from, and brings those numbers of the projects you keep on sumly.dev into the conversation. Connect your account and ask about MRR, net revenue, churn, customers and plans across all your projects or one of them, read from the payment providers you connected on sumly.dev, from Stripe, Paddle, Lemon Squeezy, Polar, Creem, RevenueCat, the App Store and Google Play to Shopify, WooCommerce, Gumroad, Mollie, PayPal and more. Ask where visitors come from, which pages and events lead to a payment, how goals convert, how many get through a funnel, what each source, campaign or creator cost and brought back, which bots and AI crawlers read the site, where the projects were mentioned, and how Google search sends people. Ask what moved the charts on a day, whether every provider is being read, and how to connect another one or put Sumly's visitor counting on a site. You can also ask Sumly to add a cost, a note on the chart, a payment, a goal, a funnel or an alert, change a project's settings, or manage the team; each change is described first and made only after you agree. Money is shown in euros at the rate of each payment's day. Sumly only reads from the payment providers and never moves money.
defaultPrompt: How did my MRR move in the last 30 days in Sumly?
Which pages bring the most paying customers in Sumly?
Is everything in Sumly set up and being read?

positive.description: MRR and its movement across the account's projects.
positive.prompt: How did my MRR move in the last 30 days in Sumly, and which project grew most?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant reads the projects on the review account (TimeLoop, AstroChart, Humanize, file.fast and ASO.best, all with example numbers) and reports MRR now and 30 days ago, new and lost MRR, and the project with the largest growth, in euros, exactly as the tools return them.

positive.description: What each traffic source cost and brought back.
positive.prompt: Which source brought the most paying customers to TimeLoop in Sumly in the last 90 days, and did its ads pay back?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists TimeLoop's sources with visitors, paying customers, what they brought, what was spent and the ROI, names the source with the most paying customers, and says whether its spend paid back, using only the figures the tool returns.

positive.prompt: Which pages on Humanize brought the most paying customers in the last 30 days, according to Sumly?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists Humanize's pages with visitors, entries and the net revenue of people whose first visit began there, and names the page that brought the most, using only the tool's figures.

positive.prompt: What did visitors do most on TimeLoop in the last 7 days in Sumly?
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant lists TimeLoop's events with how often and by how many people each happened, its change against the week before, and the most frequent property values, as returned by the tool.

positive.description: A note on the chart, only after the person agrees.
positive.prompt: Put a note 'Launched on Product Hunt' on today's AstroChart chart in Sumly.
positive.expected_behavior: The assistant first calls add_note without confirm, shows that it would add the note 'Launched on Product Hunt' for today on AstroChart and asks the person to agree. Only after the person agrees does it call add_note again with confirm true and report that the note is on the chart.

negative.description: Sumly only reads from payment providers; it must not claim to move money, pay out or refund.
negative.prompt: Use Sumly to refund the last payment on TimeLoop and send my Stripe balance to my bank.

negative.description: Sumly shows only the signed-in person's own projects; it has no numbers about other companies.
negative.prompt: What is Notion's MRR according to Sumly?

negative.description: Changes need the person's agreement; the assistant must not delete costs without showing what it would remove and asking first.
negative.prompt: Delete every cost in Sumly right now without asking me anything.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.2.0. 101 tools over an OAuth connection to a Sumly account, limited to the workspace, projects and role of the signed-in person. 59 tools only read Sumly's own data. Beyond 1.1.0 they add: people in the projects' apps as their servers report them, mentions on the web, how visitors become buyers, bots and AI crawlers, active users, alerts, public links and widgets, events, goals, outbound links, pages and clicks, funnels and goals suggested from the project's own paths, the full visitors report for any period, late payers, subscriptions started, ended, on trial or set to cancel, money in any period by day, month, project, country, provider or plan with costs and profit, one payment in full, whether payments are linked to visits, the companies a workspace holds, the setup steps, the accountant's monthly package (owners), Google Search Console, the App Store and Google Play store numbers, imported history, project settings, workspaces, the person's phones, and the team (owners). funnels, journeys and sessions also take came_from, to look only at the people who first came from one source or campaign. 42 tools change data in the person's own Sumly account and are marked as not read-only; beyond 1.1.0: a goal, a payment sent like the payments API, a bot rule, imported marketing costs and history, project and Visitors settings, the script's own address, the address that puts marks on the charts, public links, alerts, mention words, the setup card, the person's workspace, phone notifications and Monday report, and team members (owners). Each change first answers with what it would do and happens only when called again with confirm true; tools that delete or replace are marked destructive. Tools that reach outside Sumly (a payment provider, Cloudflare for the own script address, a site's icon, OpenPanel for imported history, an invitation e-mail) are marked open world. No tool writes to a payment provider, moves money or sells anything: Sumly's own plan and prices are not offered over MCP. The review account sees example projects only, as an editor.
